stem: A client reports fatigue, pallor, and shortness of breath with exertion. The complete blood count also shows a hemoglobin level below the laboratory reference range. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
rationale: NHLBI defines anemia as a condition in which the blood has a lower-than-normal amount of healthy red blood cells and notes that hemoglobin is evaluated when diagnosing anemia. Common symptoms include tiredness, paleness, weakness, and shortness of breath. Therefore A best matches both the symptom cluster and the low hemoglobin finding. Neutropenia and thrombocytopenia involve different blood-cell lines, while polycythemia is characterized by increased rather than reduced red-cell mass or hemoglobin.
educational_objective: Recognize anemia when compatible symptoms such as fatigue, pallor, and dyspnea occur together with a hemoglobin value below the laboratory reference range.
source_organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), National Institutes of Health

correction_summary: Corrected the source mismatch from a vitamin-B12-specific page to the general NHLBI anemia, symptoms, and diagnosis pages. Added a low-hemoglobin laboratory finding to eliminate ambiguity because fatigue, pallor, and exertional dyspnea alone are nonspecific. Replaced weak causal distractors with parallel hematologic conditions. Correct answer remains A; difficulty remains easy.
